title: Benchmarking Neural Network Robustness to Common Corruptions and Perturbations
publication_status_observed: ICLR 2019 (Published as a conference paper); arXiv:1903.12261v1
main_claims: ImageNet-C (15 corruption types × 5 severity levels = 75 corruptions applied to ImageNet validation images) and ImageNet-P (perturbation sequences) provide standardized, comprehensive benchmarks for evaluating image classifier robustness to common corruptions and perturbations.
There are negligible changes in relative corruption robustness from AlexNet to ResNet classifiers, indicating architectural advances have not systematically improved corruption robustness.
Some methods, including adversarial defenses (Adversarial Logit Pairing), data augmentation, and specific architectures, substantially improve corruption and perturbation robustness.
methodology: The authors apply 15 types of algorithmically generated corruptions (noise, blur, weather, digital categories) at 5 severity levels to ImageNet validation images to create ImageNet-C. They also create ImageNet-P with temporal perturbation sequences for 10 perturbation types. Performance is summarized via mean Corruption Error (mCE, normalized by AlexNet), Relative mCE, Flip Probability (FP) and Flip Rate (FR). Comparable CIFAR-10-C, CIFAR-100-C, and Tiny ImageNet-C versions are provided.
key_results: AlexNet achieves mCE = 100 (baseline); ResNet-50 achieves mCE ~76.7 on ImageNet-C, showing limited improvement in relative robustness despite large accuracy gains.
Adversarial Logit Pairing (ALP) achieves mCE ~68.8 on ImageNet-C, a substantially larger robustness improvement than purely architectural advances.
Data augmentation with the Stylized-ImageNet texture bias correction substantially improves ImageNet-C robustness.
CIFAR-10-C, CIFAR-100-C are also provided, enabling benchmarking at smaller scale.
limitations: Corruptions are algorithmically generated and may not perfectly capture all real-world distribution shifts; performance on the benchmark does not guarantee robustness to all natural corruptions.
The benchmarks should not be used for training (test set only); this constrains experimental design.
mCE is normalized by AlexNet performance on each corruption type, which introduces dependence on the baseline choice.
relevance_to_rq: Core relevance to the ood_benchmarks sub-topic: this paper introduces ImageNet-C and CIFAR-10-C, which are the primary OOD benchmarks for our study (CIFAR-10-C and CIFAR-100-C). The 15 corruption types × 5 severity levels framework, mCE metric, and the design principle of separating training from test corruptions are directly adopted in our experiment design.

key_quotes.text: Our first benchmark, IMAGENET-C, standardizes and expands the corruption robustness topic, while showing which classifiers are preferable in safety-critical applications.
key_quotes.context: Statement of purpose: ImageNet-C as the standardized corruption robustness benchmark

key_quotes.text: We find that there are negligible changes in relative corruption robustness from AlexNet classifiers to ResNet classifiers.
key_quotes.context: Key finding: architectural advances do not improve corruption robustness, motivating dedicated robustness research

key_quotes.text: we provide CIFAR-10-C, TINY IMAGENET-C, IMAGENET 64 × 64-C, and Inception-sized editions.
key_quotes.context: Availability of CIFAR-10-C as a smaller-scale benchmark directly used in our study
